title: English — Year 4 Placement
subject: english

sections.title: Tasks 1–2. Reading: Can dolphins talk?
sections.instructions:
Read the text, then choose the letter of the best answer for each question.

**Example:** Dolphins talk with ______.

a. words  b. their hands  **c. sounds** ✓
sections.passage:
**Can dolphins talk?**

Maybe they can't talk with words, but they talk with sounds. They show feelings with sounds.

Dolphins travel in a group. We call a group of fish a "school." They don't study, but they travel together. Dolphins are mammals, not fish, but they swim together in a school.

Dolphins talk to the other dolphins in the school. They give information. They tell when they are happy or sad or afraid. They say "Welcome" when a dolphin comes back to the school. They talk when they play.

They make a few sounds above water. They make many more sounds under water. People cannot hear these sounds because the sounds are very, very high. Scientists make tapes of the sounds and study them.

Sometimes people catch dolphins for a large aquarium. (An aquarium is a zoo for fish.) People can watch the dolphins in a show. Dolphins don't like to be away from their school in an aquarium. They are sad and lonely.

There are many stories about dolphins. They help people. Sometimes they save somebody's life. Dolphin meat is good, but people don't like to kill them. They say that dolphins bring good luck. Many people believe this.

sections.title: Task 3. Noun or Verb
sections.instructions:
Look at the marked word in each sentence and then choose whether it is used as a **NOUN** or a **VERB**.

**Example:**
People cannot hear these sounds because the **sounds** are very, very high. — **NOUN**
People cannot hear these sounds because they **sound** very, very high. — **VERB**

sections.title: Activity 4. Choose the right words
sections.instructions:
Read the text. Choose the right word for each gap.

**Example:** Dolphins are like small whales and some of them have ______ than 100 teeth! (many / **more** / most)
sections.passage:
**Dolphins**

Dolphins are like small whales and some of them have **more** *(Example)* than 100 teeth! Dolphins don't need to drink because (1) ______ is lots of water in the fish that they eat.

Dolphins sometimes play (2) ______ people in the water and they swim in front of boats too.

Dolphins (3) ______ in the sea in families and the parents teach (4) ______ babies to catch fish. They learn very quickly!

Dolphins can't say words, (5) ______ they can 'sing' and 'talk'. They're very clever!

*This story is about a penguin family. The penguins are hungry….*

**Now you continue the story.**
questions.criteria:
Award the point if the student writes 20 or more words continuing the story shown in the pictures (a fisherman comes, goes fishing, catches fish and the hungry penguins get food — any reasonable version of these events is fine).
The writing must be on topic (penguins / fisherman / fishing) and mostly understandable.
Accept minor spelling and grammar errors typical for Year 4; do not penalise them if meaning is clear.
Give 0 points if the text is under 20 words, off topic, or incomprehensible.
